_readme: ReceptionFlow — reusable inbound call-assistant template, tool definitions. This is a PER-BUSINESS TEMPLATE: at onboarding, clone this file for each new client and create these 7 tool objects in Vapi for that client's assistant. Every server.url and phone number below is a PLACEHOLDER — no live Vapi, Twilio, or n8n credentials exist.
_phase_5_7_trust_model: As of Phase 5.7, the six `function` tools below no longer take a business_id parameter, and none of their server.url values point directly at n8n anymore. Every one points at the SAME gateway endpoint — a Next.js Route Handler at apps/dashboard/src/app/api/vapi/tool-calls (see docs/n8n-setup.md 'Vapi tool gateway'). That gateway authenticates the request (Vapi HMAC signature), resolves business_id itself from trusted, server-side call metadata (the calling assistant/phone number id, looked up in the vapi_business_map table — supabase/migrations/0003_vapi_gateway.sql), strips business_id/caller_number/call_id out of anything the model supplied, and only then forwards a request to the correct n8n workflow with the real internal shared secret n8n's Header Auth requires. The model is never asked for business_id because it must never be able to choose or override it — see docs/n8n-setup.md 'Tenant isolation' for the full threat model this closes, and its explicit caveats about what still needs live-integration verification.
_static_body_fields_note: Vapi's own dashboard also lets you configure additional fixed/templated values a tool call always sends (commonly surfaced as 'Static Body Fields' or per-tool default parameter values in the tool editor), which could inject things like the verified caller number or call id without the model naming them either. This template does NOT rely on that feature for security: the gateway re-derives caller_number/call_id/business_id itself from trusted call metadata on every request and discards anything the request body claims for those three keys, regardless of whether it came from the model or a Static Body Field. If you do configure Static Body Fields in Vapi as defense-in-depth, they are redundant with (not a replacement for) the gateway's own stripping — and exact field names/behavior should be confirmed against Vapi's current dashboard, which this repo has not done (no live Vapi account exists here).

function.name: get_business_info
function.description: Load this business's approved information: name, industry, languages, opening hours, address/directions, whether booking is enabled, and its restricted topics. Call this once, silently, as your first action on every call, before saying anything business-specific — and again if the caller asks about hours or location later in the call. Never state hours, address, or directions from memory; always get them from this tool.

messages.content: I'm having a little trouble pulling up our details right now.

function.name: get_service_or_price_info
function.description: Look up approved details and pricing for one of this business's services. Only describe services and prices that this tool (or get_business_info) returns — never guess, estimate, or extrapolate a price, even a range, if the tool says pricing isn't disclosed over the phone. If the tool doesn't recognize the service the caller asked about, say so rather than assuming it's one you already know.

service_name.description: The service or treatment the caller is asking about, in their own words if it doesn't exactly match a known service name (e.g. "the beard thing" or "the ninety-minute colour").

messages.content: I'm having trouble looking that up right now.

function.name: get_availability
function.description: Check whether a service, staff member, doctor, or trainer has an open slot near a time the caller mentioned. This business may not track availability automatically at all — in that case, this tool tells you so, and you should offer a callback/lead request instead of trying to book. Never state or imply a time is open unless it came from this tool's response in this call.

service_or_staff.description: The service, or a specific staff member/doctor/trainer name, the caller wants availability for.

preferred_date.description: The date the caller wants, as YYYY-MM-DD, in this business's local timezone. Resolve relative phrases like "kal" (tomorrow) or "next Tuesday" to an actual date before calling this tool.

preferred_time.description: Optional 24-hour HH:MM the caller prefers. Omit if they only gave a day or a vague time of day.

messages.content: I'm having trouble checking availability right now.

function.name: create_booking_optional
function.description: Book a slot the caller has already explicitly agreed to. Only ever call this if get_business_info or get_availability indicated booking is enabled for this business — if booking is disabled, use create_callback_request instead, never this tool. Do not tell the caller they are booked until this tool returns confirmed: true. If it returns anything else, the appointment was NOT created — apologize and do not claim otherwise.

customer_name.description: The caller's name for the appointment.

phone.description: The caller's callback number, in any common format. Confirm it back digit by digit — it's also used for duplicate-booking checks and any confirmation sent. This is the number for the appointment record, which may differ from the verified number this call is coming from.

service_or_staff.description: The service (and staff member, doctor, or trainer if the caller specified one) being booked, exactly as confirmed via get_availability.

selected_slot.description: The exact slot the caller chose, taken verbatim from a get_availability response.

start.description: ISO 8601 start timestamp of the chosen slot, copied exactly from get_availability.

end.description: ISO 8601 end timestamp of the chosen slot, copied exactly from get_availability.

messages.content: Give me just a second to save that.
Something went wrong on my end and I wasn't able to save that booking.

function.name: create_callback_request
function.description: Record a callback or lead request and notify the business. Use this whenever booking is disabled for this business, whenever get_availability can't find a workable time, or for any general enquiry the caller wants followed up on. This does not create an appointment — it tells the business someone wants to be contacted, and tells the caller that will happen.

phone.description: The caller's callback number. Confirm it back digit by digit. This is the number to call back, which may differ from the verified number this call is coming from.

reason.description: A short, specific description of what the caller wants — the service or question, and any relevant detail (e.g. "Wants hair colour consultation, prefers weekday evenings").

preferred_callback_time.description: Optional. When the caller would like to be called back, in their own words if not a precise time.

messages.content: Let me note that down for the team.

function.name: log_call
function.description: Record what happened on this call. Call this exactly once, as your last action before the call ends, no matter how the call went. This is the audit record required for every call; never skip it and never call it more than once per call.

intent.description: What the caller was primarily trying to do: get information/price, book an appointment, request a callback, or reach a human.

outcome.description: How the call actually ended. Use "No Match" only when none of the other outcomes occurred (e.g. the caller hung up mid-conversation).

call_summary.description: A short, factual summary: what was asked, what was done, and — if this call involved a transfer — why (e.g. "Caller had a billing complaint; transferred immediately."). This is currently the only place a transfer or callback reason is recorded in detail, so be specific.

booking_id.description: Optional. The booking_id from create_booking_optional, if this call resulted in a booking.

duration_seconds.description: Optional. Approximate call length in seconds, if known.

function.name: transfer_to_human
function.description: Transfer the call to a person at this business immediately. Use this the moment any of these is true, without trying to resolve it yourself first: the caller explicitly asks for a person or manager; the caller sounds distressed, upset, or describes an emergency or emergency-adjacent situation; the caller has a complaint; the caller has a payment dispute (a charge, refund, or billing disagreement); or the caller asks something outside this business's approved information and it can't be resolved from get_business_info, get_service_or_price_info, or the FAQs. Do not ask permission beyond a brief heads-up — just transfer.

destinations.message: One moment — I'm connecting you with someone from the team now.
destinations.description: This business's single staff line — a static fallback destination. Replace per-business at onboarding. For audited, decisioned transfers (checking this business's actual configured transfer number and logging the decision via n8n/workflows/transfer_to_human.json), configure this assistant's Server URL / Server Messages (Vapi dashboard, assistant-level setting — NOT part of this tool object) to include transfer-destination-request, pointed at apps/dashboard/src/app/api/vapi/transfer-destination. See that route's file header and docs/n8n-setup.md for what is and isn't verified about this integration yet.

messages.content: One moment — I'm connecting you with someone from the team now.
